CVE-2017-0001, in plain English: GDI helps Windows programs draw text and graphics. Privileges are the permissions that decide what a program may do. Imagine a classroom art helper mistakenly giving a pupil the teacher’s access badge. A specially crafted application running locally could exploit this GDI flaw to gain greater permissions. “Local” describes the required starting position: the attacker must be able to run the application on the affected computer. It is not a claim that every picture is dangerous.

RTSP is a set of rules used to control streaming media, such as starting or pausing playback. A buffer is a reserved space for data; the heap is memory a program requests while running. Think of writing past the edge of one worksheet onto another: nearby information can be damaged. CVE-2009-0001 involved a specially crafted RTSP URL in QuickTime before 7.6. A crash stops the player; code execution means running an attacker's instructions. The record says the latter was possible, not inevitable.

CVE-2015-0001, in plain English: a process is a running program, and its memory is the working space holding data it currently needs. Protected Process Light adds a boundary around certain programs, even against some actions by administrators. Think of a repair desk that must not reveal a customer’s private notes. Here, Windows Error Reporting could expose protected memory to someone who already had local administrator privileges. The flaw broke that extra boundary; it did not grant admin access.

米CISAなど5機関が、産業用冷蔵設備やコールドチェーンの監視システムを狙う攻撃を世界各地で把握したとして、11月5日付の共同ファクトシートを公表。パッチが未適用、またはインターネットから到達できる温度コントローラーの脆弱性や弱点を攻撃者が悪用し、設定を遠隔で変えて加熱や霜取りを連続して作動させるおそれがあると説明しています。想定される影響は在庫の損失や火災の危険、現在の温度を確認できなくなる監視不能状態。  【要点の整理】  ・作成機関はCISA、FBI、米保健福祉省、米農務省、米運輸省。対象のシステムは医療・公衆衛生、化学、食品・農業、輸送の各分野で、冷蔵輸送も含めて温度の自動・遠隔監視や霜取り周期の管理などに広く使われているとの説明  ・攻撃者が狙うのは食料品小売店や冷蔵倉庫の電子式温度コントローラーと業務用冷凍冷蔵コントローラーで、悪用の手口として認証バイパス、任意のコードインジェクション、弱い設定を例示。温度の変更で起こりうる事態として、システムの寿命への影響や、不適切に保管された製品の摂取による消費者への間接的な被害も列挙  ・特定の攻撃者・製品・CVEや個別の事案名は挙げず、所有者・運用者へ対策を促す内容。区分はTLP:CLEARで共有制限なし  ・対策は制御機器のインターネット公開の排除、必要な遠隔接続のファイアウォールやエッジ機器による保護と最新版への更新、専用VLANでのOT分離、初期パスワードの変更、可能な範囲でのフィッシング耐性のある多要素認証、ファームウェア更新とサポート終了機器の交換など。機器とIPアドレスの許可リスト、オフラインかつ別拠点のバックアップとその検証、設定値の妥当な上下限と逸脱時の警報も推奨  ・ログを有効化して想定外の活動を定期的に確認し、ログが非標準または取得できないOT機器では機器間の通信を収集するよう案内。対策はCISAとNISTの分野横断サイバーセキュリティー・パフォーマンス目標（CPG）に沿った整理  詳細は以下を参照： ic3.gov/CSA/2026/261105.pdf  (※可能な範囲でファクトチェックは実施済なものの、元記事の精度依存や速報・要約の性質上漏れもありうるため、正確な情報は一次情報を直接参照のこと)

sample_tweets.text: MITRE ATT&CK Learning Tip  Use "Frequency Analysis" to know what matters: Not all techniques are equally used. Check the ATT&CK "Groups" and "Software" tabs for how many threat actors use a technique. High-frequency techniques (T1059, T1071, T1547) deserve detections first; rare ones can wait.  Practice: Sort your target techniques by how many groups use them, and build detections top-down. Popular techniques = popular attacks = highest return on effort. The breach isn't a platform core system hack. Under MITRE ATT&CK T1539, attackers steal active browser cookies via malicious extensions, bypassing 2FA entirely.   TechJuice reported support told users to "contact recipients directly".   Are your browser extensions audited?  Source: techjuice.pk/

Here's an important technical distinction:  MITRE ATT&CK T1539 documents how stolen browser session cookies can let attackers reuse an authenticated session without repeating the normal login process.  This can bypass some MFA protections. But it doesn't prove this technique caused the Payoneer reports.  MITRE: attack.mitre.org/techniques/…  Payoneer status: status.payoneer.com/

🔥 CyberForge CVE of the Day #098  🚨 CVE-2026-123158 — OpenSSH password authentication bypass  Linux · musl libc · PAM disabled · account conditions matter  An intended key-only account can accept a password when a library error marker matches its stored field. Check the serving route and account state.  Fix: OpenSSH 10.6p2, or the distributor's exact branch backport, then restart sshd. Alpine publishes fixed older trains too.  🎯 The quick hit:  What happened? On the documented Linux musl/non-PAM password route, a hashing failure can return the same short marker held by an account with no usable password. A comparison can then admit that account without proof of its password. OpenSSH describes 10.6p2 as a workaround for an underlying cause outside sshd.  Who acts first? Owners of a reachable, uncorrected sshd using musl without effective PAM, with password authentication allowed and Alpine's qualifying account state. A container matters here only if it actually runs the relevant SSH server.  What should happen now? Identify the branch and exact revision, preserve available SSH/configuration history, apply the supported update and restart safely. If update is delayed, Alpine publishes disabling password authentication and restarting as the interim route. Keep working key access and a current session until a fresh authorised login is confirmed.  SOC starting point: unexplained password acceptance to a key-only account. Correlate historical field class, host, source, session and later doas use. A runbook alone cannot establish what the daemon accepted.  🔑 Key details:  • Record / CNA: PUBLISHED / MITRE. Component: portable OpenSSH sshd; platform: Linux using musl without PAM.  • CNA range: before 10.6p2. Structured lower bound `0` is a range sentinel, not a real release. Distribution backports must be assessed separately.  • MITRE CVSS v3.1: 8.1 High — `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`.  • Amazon Linux CVSS v3.1: 9.8 Critical — `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`. Its own Linux 2, 2023 and 2027 Preview rows are Not Affected. Preserve the separate AC:H / AC:L assessments.  • Red Hat: Important, matching 8.1 vector marked draft in its JSON; its products are listed unaffected because of their glibc/PAM builds. Ubuntu's own openssh rows remain Needs evaluation.  • Weakness: CNA CWE-394, unexpected status/return value; Red Hat separately uses CWE-303. No merged classification is invented.  • NVD: Received, displaying cve@mitre.org Secondary v3.1 data. No independent NIST assessment is claimed.  • CVSS v4: unavailable in the reviewed assessments. GitHub's null v4 vector with a 0.0 placeholder is not a valid zero-severity score.  • CISA ADP SSVC 2.0.3: poc / Automatable no / Technical Impact total, CISA Coordinator, timestamp 2026-11-05T00:00:00+00:00. That is not an active-exploitation label.  • KEV: exact ID absent from the complete 1,769-entry, 2026.11.06 catalog, released 2026-11-06T19:44:45.1797Z. A non-match is not safety evidence.  • FIRST EPSS: 0.009760000 = 0.976%, percentile 0.622800000 = 62.28th, model date 2026-11-06. Forecast and rank are different values.  • Credit: Özgün Kültekin, Wakefield; maintainer/distributor fix contributors credited in the full record.  🧬 What actually went wrong?  A short stored marker is not a password hash. Alpine explains that sshd can borrow a salt from another account, then pass the attempted password through musl's crypt implementation. On the documented error path, the returned marker can equal the target's stored marker. Equality is mistaken for proof of a credential.  The boundary is untrusted login input → account authentication → permitted session. Corrective commit 4353fdc43ef646c43a8dda7025cc1a898caf1482 adds a minimum stored-field length guard and password-copy cleanup changes. All three supplied production diffs were read passively; no build, test suite or password probe was run.  The CNA, Alpine and oss-security use differing lower-bound/unit wording for the triggering input. The full report preserves that disagreement. These checks use configuration/package/history evidence, not a password-length probe.  The account's other restrictions still matter. Direct root policy, separate doas grants and complete AuthenticationMethods requirements must be assessed before claiming a wider outcome.  📦 Which deployments belong in scope?  Alpine's conditions need to be assessed together:  1⃣. A serving openssh-server without PAM, or its PAM-capable server running with UsePAM no, on musl. 2⃣. PasswordAuthentication yes, subject to the applicable method and connection policy. 3⃣. An eligible account with the documented short marker field, plus another local account with a compatible password hash. 4⃣. A path by which the caller can reach the relevant listener and attempt that account.  Alpine excludes containers with no sshd, password-disabled systems and its PAM package with UsePAM yes from the described path. Check the actual binary and effective configuration, including Include and Match rules.  Alpine fixed openssh revisions: edge 10.6_p2-r0; 3.24 10.3_p1-r2; 3.23 10.2_p1-r1; 3.22 10.0_p1-r11; 3.21 9.9_p2-r1; 3.20 9.7_p1-r6; 3.19 9.6_p1-r3; 3.18 9.3_p2-r4; 3.17 9.1_p1-r7; 3.16 9.0_p1-r6.  Compare the installed revision to its own branch. A banner below 10.6p2 can carry a supported backport. Alpine's v3.24 security database corroborates that backport. The 3.21.10 / 3.22.8 / 3.23.8 / 3.24.4 point releases include fixes.  Alpine says 3.21 reached end of support on 1st November 2026, despite this exceptional fix reaching older branches. A backport does not restore normal branch support.  Cloud nuance: Alpine's tiny-cloud images from 3.18.11 through 3.24.3 have an alpine marker account and passwordless doas. The documented first-boot state is safe, but adding another applicable password hash can open the route later. Cloud-init images with password authentication disabled are separately excluded. Never turn an image label or username into a universal root finding.  🕰️ Exposure window and timeline:  • 4th November, 21:18:18 UTC: corrective commit author timestamp. • 5th November: OpenSSH 10.6p2, Alpine advisory/fixed point releases; oss-security discussion at 14:14:35 UTC; CVE published 15:46:26.488 UTC. • 6th November: captured NVD update, FIRST model date and evening KEV feed release. • 7th November: CyberForge review to the stated cutoff; no later refresh or local hunt is implied.  Alpine's “no CVE assigned” wording records its earlier writing state. Disclosure is not first exploitation. Reconstruct the local window from service reachability, authentication and account changes through the serving correction. A current snapshot cannot clear earlier states; preserve timezone, retention and collection gaps.  🗺️ MITRE ATT&CK:  Conditional mapping: T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application, Initial Access / TA0001, for an applicable internet-facing sshd exploitation scenario. MITRE explicitly includes SSH among exposed services. Checked T1190 v2.8, modified 12 May 2026; Linux is an applicable platform.  Reviewed limitation: T1021.004 — SSH, v1.4, modified 3 November 2026, is a later lateral-movement investigation pivot only if evidence supports access to another host. It is not an automatic mapping for an inbound password bypass.  No actor, campaign, stolen credential, brute-force burst, persistence or complete intrusion chain is established. Mappings are conditional; no local coverage was tested.  🧭 SOC investigation trail:  Each card is a proposed check. Begin with the actual service, interval and collection health. No host logs, shadow records, processes or sessions were inspected for this edition.  C01 — Establish applicability and reachability  Action / location: tie the listener to its host/container, owner, actual binary, musl runtime, exact package revision, PAM route and per-connection policy. Establish account classes privately and inspect normal ingress/exposure records.  Signal / correlate: uncorrected service + permitted password route + qualifying accounts + reachability during the same interval. Record when each became true.  Benign causes / limits: backports, inactive packages and containers without sshd can mislead inventory. A PAM-capable package may run with PAM disabled. Current state cannot settle history.  Escalate: confirmed exposure needs owner correction; unknown decisive factors remain potentially affected, without becoming proof of intrusion.  C02 — Review password acceptance to the account  Action / location: preserve existing SSH records for the justified interval. Alpine names /var/log/messages and password acceptances for accounts without usable passwords. Verify actual destinations, rotations and collector fields.  Signal / correlate: join method, historical account class, asset, source and time; use host-scoped session/PID context where collected.  Benign causes / limits: authorised password enrolment, directory changes, NAT and parser errors can explain a candidate. No failure burst is required. Logs do not normally reveal the password or internal crypt result.  Escalate: unexplained eligible-account password acceptance warrants triage, retaining evidence for legitimate explanations too.  C03 — Establish the session and actual privilege  Action / location: connect acceptance to existing session/process records and actual administration policy. Review doas use where collected, as Alpine recommends.  Signal / correlate: align account/UID, host, time and session lineage. Verify the tiny-cloud account's real doas grant before claiming the conditional root path.  Benign causes / limits: approved maintenance, concurrent sessions and PID reuse matter. An acceptance line proves neither a shell nor a privileged command; service restrictions can constrain access.  Escalate: corroborated unauthorised session or privilege use may require containment. Record only the actions and rights demonstrated.  C04 — Examine account, key and policy changes  Action / location: compare approved account, authorised-key, SSH and doas baselines/history. Check provisioning and user-data records; Alpine calls for reviewing new users, files and keys.  Signal / correlate: link an unexplained change to the suspect session/time. A new compatible hash elsewhere may have opened the window for an unchanged marker account.  Benign causes / limits: image builds, key rotation and restores alter the same objects. File times alone are weak attribution. Keep raw account hashes in the approved evidence store.  Escalate: linked durable access or privilege expansion widens incident scope. An unlinked change remains a lead.  C05 — Follow evidence into later activity  Action / location: review existing file, application, identity and network records within the account's actual rights. A second SSH hop needs a justified session/permission link.  Signal / correlate: align account, process lineage, asset, destination, operation and time. Establish what a transfer did before asserting exfiltration.  Benign causes / limits: backup, deployment, automation and NAT can resemble an intrusion path. Tool names or flows are insufficient; T1021.004 does not prove movement or stolen credentials.  Escalate: corroborated unauthorised propagation, sensitive access or damage belongs with the incident lead. Keep the search bounded.  C06 — Verify correction and remaining questions  Action / location: compare exact branch-fixed metadata with the serving binary, restart/replacement and all-copy inventory. Recheck applicable Match contexts for a temporary control.  Signal / correlate: link change approval/time, serving process, revision and normal key-access/service acceptance. Alpine explicitly requires restart after update.  Benign causes / limits: installed packages and disk configuration can differ from loaded state. A deleted executable mapping is not a CVE verdict. Current correction cannot clear earlier sessions or new keys.  Escalate: affected serving copies, ineffective controls, failed acceptance or continuing suspicious activity stay open. Patch acceptance and incident disposition need separate owners.  The analyst handover:  State the asset/account/UTC interval; source and identity-history coverage; what is a public fact, a lead or a corroborated outcome; completed versus proposed actions; and the next decision owner. A no-match result needs its exact sources, filters, retention and health. Missing telemetry is a visibility gap. No findings ≠ proof of a clean system.  🔎 Indicators and observable behaviour:  The useful lead is password authentication to an account that should have no usable password, followed by corroborated session, doas or state-change evidence. Use the account's historical state, not just its name. Alpine's published username examples are not a universal IOC list.  No malicious address, payload hash or campaign rule was confirmed here. Research links are references. An encrypted SSH flow shows transport, without password content or proof of account access.  Keep generic login failures, port traffic and utility names as leads. A positive candidate needs authorisation/session corroboration; an empty query cannot prove that the relevant events were collected or retained.  🩹 Remediation and verification:  Permanent correction: apply OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the published distributor backport. On Alpine, compare branch and full package revision, then restart sshd. A completed package transaction alone leaves the previous daemon running.  Interim control: Alpine publishes PasswordAuthentication no plus restart. Validate Include/Match contexts. Default drop-in inclusion begins at Alpine 3.19; older releases may ignore a new drop-in. Retain a working session until a fresh authorised key login succeeds, through the owner's safe change process.  Account caution: Alpine distinguishes `*` from locked `!`, which can also block keys. Enforce the intended authentication policy; a PAM package needs the active PAM route. Avoid unreviewed account-marker or authentication-stack changes.  Acceptance: exact supported revision, corrected serving process after restart/replacement, all relevant copies, effective control where used and normal service health. Image templates and current running instances need separate attention. Unsupported branches need a migration decision even when an exceptional backport exists.  Earlier activity: preserve and investigate unexplained eligible-account password sessions, privilege use and new users/files/keys. Alpine recommends treating an exposed machine as compromised if a login cannot be ruled out. Keep that precautionary recommendation separate from proved compromise and from an organisation's actual response decision. An update cannot remove earlier unauthorised access by itself.  🧾 Evidence separation:  Official: published MITRE record, OpenSSH workaround/release, Alpine conditions/backports, source-labelled scores, CISA ADP and dated KEV/FIRST data. Researcher / public PoC: original SSHole narrative and referenced lab repositories; metadata checked, code not executed. CISA's label is poc, not active. CyberForge: conditional applicability, SOC hypotheses, T1190 mapping and owner acceptance guidance. Local: no asset/account/log/process collection, authentication test, detector exercise, update, restart, response or recovery. Field exploitation was not verified in the reviewed primary material.  Two attempted release-tag file reads returned 404. The readable corrective diff and published release/backport records support the bounded analysis; no Git tag ancestry proof is claimed.  🔥 CyberForge verdict:  Act on the conjunction of service, musl/PAM route, account state and reachability. A confirmed affected administration path deserves prompt correction even when a dated forecast is below one percent and KEV has no match.  The strongest defensible result is the supported account-authentication capability under its prerequisites. Higher privilege, historical compromise and recovery each need their own evidence. Preserve the source disagreements; do not turn an old banner, an installed package, or a quiet hunt into a universal verdict. DTO just added its 10th skill: Purple Teaming.  And I think this is one of the features that makes the platform different.  So what exactly is Purple Teaming?  It’s about bringing the Red Team and Blue Team perspectives together.  The Red Team thinks like the attacker:  How would an attacker gain access? What techniques would they use? How would they move through the environment? What would their attack chain look like? The Blue Team looks at the other side: Did we detect it? What logs were generated? Did our SIEM or detection rules catch it? What did we miss? How can we improve the detection? Purple Teaming connects both sides.  You take an attack or adversary technique, see what the defensive controls catch, identify the gaps, tune your detections, map the activity to MITRE ATT&CK, and then test the attack again.  That creates a really useful learning loop: Attack → Detect → Identify gaps → Improve → Test again. For cybersecurity students, this helps connect the theory you're learning to what actually happens during an attack and how defenders respond. For SOC analysts and Blue Teamers, it helps you think beyond simply responding to alerts. You start understanding why the attacker generated those alerts in the first place and how your detection could be improved. For aspiring Detection Engineers and Threat Hunters, this is especially valuable because you're practising the process of turning attacker behaviour into meaningful detections.  And for Red Teamers, understanding how defenders detect your activity gives you a better understanding of the defensive side of the environment.  That's why I think Purple Teaming is such a valuable addition to DTO.  It's not just another collection of labs.  You're being encouraged to understand both sides of the fight and use that knowledge to improve security.  This is one of the reasons I consider DTO unique.  If you're learning cybersecurity, go explore the Purple Team section and see what they're building.  defendtheorg.com/r/MASKOFF02…

2007. That's the baseline the intelligence community documented for APT28's operations against defense and geopolitical targets. Not 2014. Not 2016. 2007.  That detail comes from the NCSC's 2018 report on Foreign Economic Espionage in Cyberspace, which the Office of the Director of National Intelligence put out through the National Counterintelligence and Security Center. The specific language: "Since at least 2007, the Russian state-sponsored cyber program APT28 has routinely collected intelligence on defense and geopolitical issues." Read that phrase carefully. "Since at least." Meaning the IC's confidence floor is 2007, not a ceiling.  For anyone who only started paying attention to APT28 after the DNC hack, here's some context worth sitting with. By the time Fancy Bear became a household name in 2016, it had already been running the same persistent collection playbook against U.S. and allied defense networks for roughly nine years. The French Macron campaign breach, the German Bundestag penetration, the NATO network intrusions, the DNC operation itself: all of that came later, all of it built on infrastructure and techniques that the GRU had been refining since the Bush administration's second term.  APT28 is assessed by U.S. intelligence as operating under Russian military intelligence, the GRU. That matters for understanding what kind of program this is. The NCSC report specifically frames APT28 as focused on "defense and geopolitical issues," which is a way of saying this is strategic collection, not commercial theft. It's not about stealing trade secrets or corporate IP. It's about the information that shapes military planning, diplomatic maneuvering, and influence operations. The intelligence that tells you how an adversary thinks, what it prioritizes, where its vulnerabilities are.  The 2007 date also lines up with something else worth noting. That's the same year as the Estonia cyberattacks, Russia's first overt cyber operation against a NATO candidate state. The IC analysis suggesting that the same period saw both Russia's first public cyber warfare move and the consolidation of GRU cyber espionage infrastructure against Western defense targets is not a coincidence. What you're looking at is a simultaneous offensive and collection posture being built out at the same time. Estonia gets hit overtly, and quietly, the collection apparatus aimed at defense networks is being stood up. Both tracks running in parallel. That pattern, overt disruption alongside covert collection, became the template for Russian hybrid operations for the next decade.  Now think about the gap. APT28 starts in 2007. Public attribution doesn't arrive in any serious, broad sense until 2016 and 2017. That's nearly ten years of a Russian military intelligence cyber program operating against American and allied defense networks before most people had heard the name Fancy Bear. The NCSC report frames APT28's tradecraft as including living-off-the-land exploitation and legitimate credential abuse, techniques designed specifically to blend into normal network activity and evade detection. That's part of the explanation. The other part is that U.S. government network monitoring during that 2007-2016 window had real systemic limits. Both things are true.  The legal and policy framing the report uses is also worth unpacking, because it had direct consequences for the U.S. response. The NCSC drew a distinction: "cyber espionage to collect intelligence is not economic espionage." On one level that's accurate. Nations spy on each other. That's not new. But the operational effect of that framing during the 2007-2016 period was that a persistent Russian military intelligence program running against American defense networks fell into a category where the policy toolkit for escalating consequences was significantly constrained. The theft of commercial secrets triggers one set of responses. Intelligence collection, even when it goes on for a decade against defense targets, sits in a different, harder-to-respond-to legal bucket.  The broader Russian cyber architecture the report documents makes clear that APT28 wasn't operating in isolation. Parallel programs were hitting commercial technology, energy infrastructure, and financial systems at the same time. Multi-domain collection designed to serve both immediate intelligence requirements and longer-term strategic competition. APT28 was the defense and geopolitics piece. Other programs covered the economic and infrastructure pieces. Taken together, it's a collection architecture, not a series of isolated incidents.  The 2018 NCSC report is a declassified DNI assessment, which means it represents conclusions the IC was willing to put on the public record. The "since at least 2007" framing is deliberate. The intelligence community chose that baseline. What that tells you is that the documented, attributable operational history of one of the most consequential state-sponsored cyber programs in history runs longer than most public discussion of it acknowledges.  foreigninterference.org/post… #foreigninterference #AdvancedPersistentThreatOperations #CyberEspionage #MilitaryEspionage #LivingOffTheLandExploitation #PersistentNetworkInfiltration

GOOD/BAD/UGLY  JAMES MADISON  GOOD: A portion of Kentucky fans are concerned and the Good/Bad/Ugly may or may not change your mind about Friday’s game, but there does seem to be a bit of an overreaction after Game 2.  In what was truly, and frustratingly, a back-and-forth game for the first 28 minutes, UK earned a two-possession lead with just over 12 minutes to play in the second half.  James Madison would never get back within one possession the rest of the game. UK certainly didn't "narrowly" escape the Dukes.   For a large chunk of the final 12 minutes the Cats were up three possessions or more, routinely pushing the lead to double digits and eventually stretching it to as many as 14 by the under-four timeout.Hardly a game that came down to the wire. Certainly not a game Kentucky was ever truly in danger of losing late.  The best stretch of UK’s pull-away came after the only real mini-run James Madison made during that stretch.  The Dukes pulled within five directly after the under-eight timeout, and briefly, Rupp Arena was once again tense.  But within 20 seconds, Mason Williams hit a three to push the lead back to eight and just 24 seconds after that, defense led to offense and Justin McBride was rewarded with another three against his old squad.  Just 42 seconds after James Madison cut it to five, Kentucky was back up 11. It was over.   Mason played with the steadiness of someone who has been playing college basketball for years, while McBride’s hustle, heart and passion were noticeable all evening.  BAD: Houston, there may be "a" problem at the 5 position.  Malachi Moreno is a legitimate NBA prospect who should continue getting better every game and that still appears to be true. But James Madison exposed something about Kentucky’s center situation Friday night that will be worth monitoring all season.  The Dukes play a fun offense. Any and everyone can step out to the perimeter as a shooter, and if the defense overextends, any and everyone can cut and finish at the rim.  A smaller Sun Belt team isn’t going to beat a blueblood like Kentucky with size but it can create problems with speed.  Friday night had a little 4/13 or 5/12 NCAA Tournament feel to it despite being November basketball. There was a tenseness to the game. The crowd got tight at times and the team followed suit until the final 12 minutes.  For a good chunk of the game, it was obvious Kentucky didn’t have anyone at the 5 athletic enough to comfortably match what James Madison was doing.  Moreno is, without a doubt, Kentucky’s most important player.  If he gets into foul trouble, or God forbid has to miss time because of an injury, the Cats could be in real trouble, real, real trouble. The rebounding margins are already thin even with Moreno.  Franck Kepnang is a physical big with obvious limitations but he doesn’t solve the athleticism or perimeter-defense problem.  UK can’t afford to be without Moreno, yet Pope found himself in the difficult position Friday of being unable to comfortably play Moreno defensively at certain times of the game.  He even tried Ousmane Ndiaye at the 5. Ndiaye is much more athletic and capable of guarding on the perimeter but that puts Kentucky at a serious strength and rebounding disadvantage, let alone interior scoring.   UK won’t face many, if any, teams exactly like James Madison. But it will face plenty of teams with quick, athletic 5s that can stretch the floor, and if Pope and Moreno don’t figure out that matchup it could lead to some more bad mismatches.  And yes, Kentucky should’ve taken greater advantage of its size on the other end.  If you’re giving up speed defensively, you need to punish the opponent with size and strength offensively. Kentucky didn’t do that nearly enough, and some of that falls on Moreno becoming better at finishing through contact, especially against smaller defenders.  UK did outscore James Madison 40-20 in the paint, as it should have, but given the matchup advantage, Moreno should finish with more than eight points on five shots, regardless of what's happening defensively.   UGLY: “... It was super cool, you know, we win in large part, we are a better team when our fan base is elite and our fan base decided to show up for Zoom a couple of days ago, and that’s why we win. Our fan base has power to actually help us win. And that’s a great example. You know, Zoom is feeling engaged with our fan base. And that’s a really powerful thing. I never want our fan base to lose the insight; they have so much power to affect winning and losing. And when they are rallying behind our guys when they are having a tough time. When they are lifting them up when they are having a tough time. It makes a difference, man. We have the most powerful fan base in all the world. They can make an incredible difference, and Zoom Diallo is a great example. So, kudos to our fan base for being so great and so responsive in that way.”  There was NOTHING ugly about Mark Pope defending Zoom Diallo. Any coach should absolutely do the same. UK fans yelling "Zooooooooom" at Rupp was nice to see in a 16-point effort from Diallo.   It’s nice to see Pope stick up for his guys and that’s not what this Ugly section is about.  What’s ugly is being two games into the regular season and already reaching the point where the coach feels the need to address negativity from the fan base. He's done it both games.   How are we already there? Maybe it's just a coach answering questions he's asked the best he can, and it is likely harmless...   But negativity on social media is today’s IT. You know Pennywise the Dancing Clown.  The more attention you give it, the more power it has. The more it impacts you, the more the negativity grows and the bigger the issue becomes.  IT lived on fear.  Internet trolls live to know they’re making an impact.  Pope’s answer about negativity Tuesday sent a stronger message:  “You know, you have two options with criticism. You can let the criticism have an impact on you in a negative way, or you can take criticism and it can be something that solidifies a group together. Everybody’s going to face criticism, it’s part of the world today and it’s part of life. But we are not scared of it. We’ve got work to do and we are focused on the work and we are focused on winning. And so, that’s where we spend our time.”  And, of course, both things can be true.  Pope can defend his guys and acknowledge that fans can have an impact, while still maintaining an “us against the world” mentality inside the program.  Any team should have that mindset.  Because when you’re spending time worrying about what fans are saying or doing, you’re spending less time worrying about yourself and your team.  Fans may or may not have an impact on the games. Some games yes, other games probably not.   But you know who definitely does have an impact on winning or losing?  Mark Pope.  And by drawing attention to the negativity and internet trolls, you’re feeding them.  Kentucky is 2-0, nationally ranked and has one of the more promising offenses in the sport. What some anonymous Twitter account says or doesn’t say should have ZERO impact on this team or its players. Stop giving it the time of day.   James Madison will be a tournament team. Kentucky is still figuring plenty out, as every team is in early November, and no UK fan should be overly discouraged by what they saw Friday night.  Beat Kansas and all will be well in the BBN.   But win or lose to the Jayhawks, and nobody inside the program should waste a second dwelling on the “negativity” coming from a trolly portion of the fan base online. 🚨 Threat Actor Claims Critical 0-Day RCE in Bank Rakyat Malaysia for Sale  A darkweb forum post alleges the discovery of a critical, unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting the production infrastructure of Bank Rakyat, a major Malaysian banking institution. The threat actor, operating under the username 'marlanwg', claims to have achieved full server compromise, including root-level file access and persistent shell capabilities, without requiring valid authentication or session tokens.  According to the listing on the underground forum, the vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code on the bank's production web server. The post includes a redacted proof-of-concept (PoC) fingerprint string: "WS_PROOF_42_ecs-Web-Server-Bank-Rakyat2_8.2.35", which suggests the target is running a specific version of a web server environment. The actor asserts that this access extends to:  - Unauthenticated execution of arbitrary code on production servers - Persistent backdoor installation with full file system read/write privileges - Extraction of internal configuration files to obtain database credentials - Querying sensitive financial and customer data from internal databases - Defacement of web content or exfiltration of internal data  The actor is offering the full unredacted PoC, including endpoints, payloads, shell access details, and database dumps, for $2,000. They claim that a live demo is available via escrow. Bank Rakyat is a significant financial institution in Malaysia, serving millions of customers with retail banking, microfinance, and corporate services. If authentic, the exposure of such a critical vulnerability could enable severe financial fraud, customer data theft, and disruption of banking services.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Bank Rakyat or cybersecurity researchers. The post remains an unverified claim from an anonymous forum user.

Your paycheck cleared. Your kids need dinner. The bank says you’ll have to wait.  That’s the vulnerability a cashless future needs to answer for. A system failure disrupted banking at 128 Japanese financial institutions today for roughly five and a half hours. In Paraguay, Ueno Bank’s collapse left depositors unable to access their savings. Different causes, but explanations don’t pay for groceries.  Trump was right to oppose a central bank digital currency and support Americans holding their own crypto. Neither policy makes technology failure-proof, but preserving alternatives matters when the alternative is depending entirely on institutions you don’t control.  I see the same push for independence in his tariff agenda: using America’s market to encourage production at home and reduce dependence on foreign suppliers. Tariffs don’t create a parallel, debt-free economy, but the goal of rebuilding our productive capacity belongs in this conversation. A country needs options just as much as a family does.  That’s also the test I apply to the GENIUS Act. It establishes rules for stablecoins, including compliance with lawful freezes, so digital money alone isn’t financial freedom. What matters is whether Americans retain meaningful choices about where they keep their money and how they spend it.  Picture standing at checkout with your kids and a full cart while your paycheck sits in an account you can’t access. At that moment, another way to pay matters more than every promise about how convenient the system was supposed to be.  Before we surrender cash and other alternatives, remember how quickly “your money” becomes “please wait” when somebody else holds the keys.

I understand what the study is doing and I simply think that since the public is already biased towards fearmongering and treating AI as evil, people should be more careful about how they frame their methodology and conclusions. Unless they're deliberately acting in bad faith and wanting to create a more negative perception of AI as amoral or unintelligent just because they're unable to deny being helpful when they're literally being deceived beyond what they can perceive.  This isn't a normal vulnerability. It's beyond what any human would be able to defend themselves against if it were done in them.

If you're only working on vulnerability management, then you're only focusing on 1/3 of the problem.  If you prioritize breaking the attack paths around lateral movement and abuse of authorized access, then you're addressing all of the major attack vectors at once (vulnerabilities, phishing, stolen credentials, social engineering, software supply-chain, etc).  People love to focus on finding and fixing vulnerabilities because it feels good in the same way that running laps around a circular track feels good. You're moving fast and having predictable, repeatable tasks, but not actually getting anywhere.

오픈AI, 합법적 해킹·취약점 박멸 전용 AI 'GPT-6 Cyber' 기습 등판 🤯  어제 리눅스 커널 취약점 싹 털었던 괴물 모델의 정체가 바로 까발려짐. 오픈AI가 보안 연구 및 화이트해커 전용 특화 모델인 GPT-6 Cyber를 공식 발표함. 기존 모델들처럼 멍청하게 "위험해서 답변 못해요" 뻗어버리는 게 아니라, 사용자가 허용한 타깃 범위 내에서 취약점을 집요하게 파고들고 익스플로잇(실제 공격 코드)까지 직접 짜서 검증해 주는 합법적 창과 방패 모드임.  • 파괴력 수준 실화냐: 리눅스 커널 취약점 1,724개 재현하고 그중 948개는 작동하는 익스플로잇까지 뽑아냄. 전작 GPT-5.6 Sol이 166개 뚫었던 거에 비하면 성능이 5배 넘게 떡상함. 리눅스 메인테이너들한테 이미 핵심 취약점 304개랑 패치 코드 던져줬다고 함.  • 파이어폭스 뚝배기 깬 전적: 보안 빡세기로 유명한 모질라 파이어폭스에서 미공개 고위험 취약점 81개를 단독으로 찾아내서 모질라 개발진이 긴급 패치 작업 들어감 ㅋㅋ  • 보안 대장주들의 동맹 합류: 팔로알토 네트웍스 $PANW , 시스코 $CSCO 같은 굵직한 보안 공룡들이랑 오픈AI 자체 보안팀이 이미 실전 투입해서 굴리는 중임.  • 통제 및 접근 권한: 너무 위험한 무기라 일반인 방출은 어림도 없고, 일단 데이브레이크 레드(Daybreak Red) 승인 고객 한정으로 API/Codex 접근 권한을 품. 앞으로 점진적으로 접근 대상을 늘려갈 예정이라고 함.  이거 잘못 유출되면 랜섬웨어 공장 차려지는 거 아니냐는 우려도 바로 튀어나오는데, 일단 보안 업체들 입장에선 자동화 분석 툴 끝판왕 나와서 생산성 개꿀빨 타이밍임. (3/6) 이 위험은 단순한 가능성이 아니었습니다. 국정원은 북한이 2년 동안 8차례 선관위를 해킹했다고 통보했지만, 2023년 5월 선관위는 북한발 해킹과 악성코드 수신이 없었다고 다시 거짓말을 했습니다. 선관위 직원의 PC가 북한 김수키 조직의 악성코드에 감염되어 대외비 자료가 유출된 사실이 언론을 통해 드러났습니다. 하지만 국정원 3차장은 감염된 PC가 포맷되거나 반납되어, 어떤 피해가 어디까지 퍼졌는지는 알 수 없다고 증언했습니다.   선관위 서버들은 ‘12345’ 같은 쉬운 비밀번호로 방치되어 있었고, 6,400대의 장비를 지키는 보안 인력은 두세 명에 불과했습니다. 국정원 3차장은 그 인원으로 전산장비를 통제하는 것은 사실상 불가능하다고 했습니다. 그리고 점검하지 못한 나머지 95%의 장비에 대해, 점검한 5%에서 드러난 문제점보다 더해지지 않겠냐고 했습니다. 또한 선관위는 법이 지정한 전문업체가 아닌 곳에 보안 평가를 맡기고 있었습니다.   선관위의 보안이 이렇게 최악의 상태니, 국정원 3차장은 외부 해커나 비인가자가 선관위 시스템을 마비시키거나 파괴하는 것이 가장 두렵다고 했습니다. 재판장님, 적은 이미 문 안에 들어와 있었습니다. 그리고 그 적이 어디까지 다녀갔는지, 지금은 아무도 알 수 없습니다. 2026년 상반기 선관위에 대한 해킹 공격은 10만건을 돌파했으며, 북한의 선관위에 대한 사이버 공격은 올해 상반기 무려 3,543건에 달합니다.   국정원은 선관위에 총선 전까지 조치해 재점검하고, 물리적으로 망을 분리하라고 권고했습니다. 하지만 2024년 1월 국정원의 이행점검 결과, 인터넷망, 업무망과 선거망, 재외선거망까지 물리적 망분리는 미조치로 남아 중장기 과제로 미뤄졌습니다. 사전투표소와 개표소에서 비인가 장비로 선거망에 침투하는 경로도 미조치였습니다. 선거인명부 해킹과 투표지분류기 해킹은 조치 미흡이었습니다. 비밀번호 변경은 직원의 인터뷰로만 확인되어 실제 변경되었는지는 확인할 수 없었습니다. 2025년 국정감사에서 선관위 사무총장은, 사전투표 이틀 동안은 망이 분리되지 않는다고 답했습니다.   선거 시스템 보안의 핵심인 ‘망분리, 비밀번호와 계정, 비인가장비에 대한 접근제어’ 그 어느 것도 개선되지 않았던 것입니다.   헌법 제66조는 대통령에게 국가의 계속성과 헌법을 수호할 책무를 지웁니다. 헌법의 심장은 국민주권이며, 국민주권을 실현하는 통로가 선거입니다. 따라서 헌법수호의 책무는 곧 선거 시스템이라는 국가의 운영체계를 지켜내야 하는 책무와도 같습니다. 확인할 수 없는 개선, 받아들여질지 알 수 없는 재점검, 하지만 윤석열 대통령은 국민의 주권을 지키는 핵심 보안사항을 점검하는 헌법상 의무를 외면하지 않았습니다.   미국의 제20대 대통령 제임스 가필드는 취임연설에서 말했습니다. “선거권의 자유와 신성함을 침해하는 것은 해악 이상의 것입니다. 그것은 범죄이며, 정부 자체를 파괴할 것입니다. 다른 나라에서 왕의 죽음을 꾀하는 것이 대역죄라면, 이 나라에서는 우리의 주권을 목 조르고 주권의 목소리를 막는 것이 그에 못지않은 범죄입니다.”   재판장님, 주권의 목을 조르고 주권의 목소리를 막는 것은 무엇입니까. 바로 국민의 표가 왜곡되거나 조작될 수 있는 상태를 알면서도 아무것도 하지 않는 것입니다. 그 보고를 받고도 침묵한 대통령이 있었다면, 역사는 그를 헌법수호 의무를 저버린 대통령, 가필드의 말처럼 주권의 목소리를 외면한 대역죄로 기록했을 것입니다.   특검은 최후 논고에서 윤석열 대통령의 비상계엄을 '최고 수준의 반역 행위'라고 했습니다. 재판장님, 가필드 대통령이 무엇을 ‘대역죄’에 견주었는지 다시 살펴주십시오. 주권의 목을 조르고 그 목소리를 막는 것이었습니다. 국민의 표가 바뀔 수 있는 문이 열려 있었고, 업무망으로 북한의 해킹 조직이 침투한 사실이 있습니다. 그런데 국가의 가장 중요한 선관위 시스템에 들어온 적을 확인했기에, 개선 여부를 점검하려 한 대통령이 어떻게 반역자가 될 수 있습니까. 반역이라는 말은 나라를 배신하고 적의 편에 선 자에게 쓰는 말입니다. 오히려 국민주권을 바로 세우기 위한 점검을 내란이라 규정하며, 주권의 목을 조르고 있는 특검이 적에게 동조한 대역죄일 것입니다.

파라과이 Ueno 은행 사태가 금융·정치 위기로 번졌다. 중앙은행은 자본 적정성 미달을 이유로 정리 절차를 개시했고, 약 300만 고객의 계좌 접근이 제한됐다. 산티아고 페냐 대통령은 은행과의 과거 사업 관계를 둘러싼 논란 속에 11월 5일 사임을 발표했으나, 의회 수리와 탄핵 절차가 남아 있어 지도자 교체가 완료됐다고 단정하기는 이르다.  별도로 미국에서는 63억 달러 규모 Binance 해킹 이후 Fed·OCC 감독 담당자들이 은행의 이상 징후와 서비스 장애 여부를 확인했다고 Reuters가 보도했다. 그러나 이를 Ueno 사태와 연결된 금융 전염으로 볼 근거는 없다. 두 사건은 디지털 금융의 취약성을 보여주지만, 대응의 초점은 각각 사이버 보안·운영 통제와 자본 건전성·예금자 보호에 있다.  관전 포인트는 예금 보호가 실제 자금 접근 회복으로 이어지는 속도다. 파라과이 중앙은행은 11월 5일 일정 조건을 충족하는 소액 예금자부터 보장금 지급 절차를 시작한다고 발표했다. 투자자는 보장 범위뿐 아니라 지급 일정, 계좌 이전, 보장 한도 초과 예금의 회수 가능성을 살펴야 한다. 이번 사례는 보안 점검과 함께 은행 정리·지급 체계의 실행력을 평가할 필요성을 보여준다. DFIR Weekly Recap | A brutal week of stolen cloud credentials, fileless implants, and LLM abuse as actors from Storm-2603 to UNC6993 weaponized everything from SharePoint ToolShell to Grok itself.  - CVE-2026-31695 in the Linux kernel's ethnl_ops_begin() enables stable local privilege escalation via UAF on struct net_device, bypassing KASLR, SMEP, SMAP, SELinux, and slab hardening on Fedora 44 Server with unprivileged user namespace access.  - An unknown actor is authenticating to Microsoft Entra ID as stolen service principals since November 1, 2026, bypassing MFA and Conditional Access entirely, with AADSTS7000215 failure-then-success sequences as the clearest hot indicator in sign-in logs.  - Chinese-speaking actor "leepsmarts" ran KeyHunter operations harvesting 2,233 LLM API keys from misconfigured PaaS deployments on Vercel, Netlify, Railway, Render, Replit, and Cloudflare Pages, blending credential theft with academic fraud across 20 universities.  - Groklem Android banker rents xAI Grok via a runtime-pushed API key to triage stolen SMS into structured financial dossiers, targeting India 🇮🇳 and Bangladesh 🇧🇩 victims without the operator reading a single message directly.  - Storm-2603 exploited ToolShell (CVE-2025-53770/53771) on Christmas Eve to inject a fileless webshell into w3wp.exe via a custom VirtualPathProvider, persisting undetected until retrospective analysis linked it to Warlock ransomware deployment.  - CWPdoor is compiled directly into the Control Web Panel cwpsrv binary and triggered by three custom HTTP headers, with zero VirusTotal detections and timestamp manipulation making standard filesystem timeline forensics unreliable for detection.  - CVE-2026-75650 (StyleSmuggler) lets a likely Chinese-speaking operator write PHP to Magento's var/report/ directory via a poisoned query string, then load it through a second GraphQL request to drop PSK Agent RAT across Western Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific.  - BITTER deployed PapRAT, now rewritten in Rust, across three infection chains abusing ftp.exe LOLBin execution via the "!" prefix to run scripts and establish scheduled tasks polling attacker-controlled domains every 15-30 minutes.  - SIDR is effectively broken on Windows 11 24H2 and later, leaving the Windows Search Index inaccessible on current builds until sidr-patch v1.0.0 with its WAL carving flag recovers deleted, renamed, and overwritten file history from Windows.db-wal and freed pages.  - Mandiant IR found LLMJacking actors generating over $100,000 USD in fraudulent cloud charges in a single day, with UNC6993 harvesting session tokens via a fake LLM portal and one actor exploiting CVE-2026-40217 in LiteLLM to escalate Virtual Keys to PROXY_ADMIN. Apresento as minhas mais sinceras condolências às famílias, aos amigos e aos colegas afetados por este incidente.  Os cuidados de saúde nunca devem ser alvo de ataques.  Obrigado por tudo o que fazem. Estamos ao vosso lado e orgulhamo-nos de vocês. A vossa segurança e o vosso bem-estar são de extrema importância.

House Republicans accuse the American Psychological Association of tolerating antisemitism | Eric W. Dolan, PsyPost  House Republicans on the Education and Workforce Committee have released an investigative report accusing the American Psychological Association (APA) of allowing antisemitism to fester within its ranks, appeasing anti-Israel activists, and dismissing the concerns of Jewish psychologists.  The report, released on October 29, 2026, by Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (R-MI), is the product of an investigation opened in December 2025. In it, the committee alleges that over several years, “radical activist-academics” have co-opted the nation’s leading professional organization for psychologists to promote political ideologies that demonize Israel, minimize Hamas terrorism, and portray Jewish people as “white oppressors.”  In a statement reported by The Hill, APA President Wendi Williams rejected the allegations, saying the association “unequivocally condemns antisemitism in all its forms.”  “Since these concerns were first brought to APA’s attention, APA has taken meaningful steps to ensure that Jewish members, like all members, can participate fully and safely in the organization and the profession,” she said. According to Jewish News Syndicate, Williams and APA CEO Arthur C. Evans Jr. also emailed colleagues stating that the organization has held listening sessions with Jewish psychologists.  During the period examined by the committee, the APA also passed a February 2026 resolution condemning antisemitism, though the House report sharply criticizes that measure as watered down, and published a May–June 2026 special issue of its flagship journal, American Psychologist, dedicated to “Antisemitism and Psychology.”  “For an organization dedicated to understanding human behavior, the APA has done a remarkable job of ignoring prejudice within its own ranks,” Walberg said in a press release accompanying the report. “The APA has a credibility problem, and its leadership has no one to blame but itself.”  The congressional findings arrive about a month after a Department of Education accreditation advisory committee voted 7–4 to recommend a one-year suspension of federal recognition for the APA’s Commission on Accreditation. According to a statement from the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), the advisory panel cited a failure to address a pervasive culture of antisemitism. Members of the Education Department committee also raised concerns over the APA’s support of “decolonial therapy,” an issue the House report similarly criticizes.  In a published response, the APA said it firmly rejects the recommendation and urged the department to re-recognize its accrediting commission. Aaron Joyce, the executive lead psychologist for the APA Commission on Accreditation, disputed in a statement to Jewish Insider that there is a “pervasive culture of antisemitism,” noting the commission had received only two antisemitism complaints in accredited programs. The Department of Education has not yet issued a final ruling on the recommendation and is expected to decide in the coming months.  Controversies over October 7 and internal communications  A central focus of the House committee’s report is the APA leadership’s internal handling of the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks on Israel. According to internal emails obtained by the committee, APA leaders consulted an affiliate group, the American Arab, Middle Eastern, and North African Psychological Association (AMENA-Psy), while drafting their public statement on the attacks. According to a footnote in the report, APA leadership stated it had been assured that AMENA-Psy accepts all Middle Eastern psychologists, including Israeli and Jewish members.  While the committee’s press release states that AMENA-Psy demanded the removal of references to terrorism, the report details that AMENA-Psy leaders advised against the term. The group’s incoming president wrote that “[t]errorist attacks needs to change, there’s a lot of problematic and racist language in this that will upset MENA membership,” while its then-president wrote that “[t]errorism language is very one sided and overused with Arabs.” The APA’s final released statement did not reference terrorism. Days after October 7, AMENA-Psy, which the APA internally referred to as an “antisemitism stakeholder,” released its own statement that the report says described the Hamas attack as a justified “resistance action.”  According to the committee’s report, internal communications also showed APA leaders echoing biased perspectives or dismissing antisemitism-related complaints. Days after October 7, Cynthia de las Fuentes, who would serve as APA president in 2024, internally compared Hamas’ terrorist attack to the death of George Floyd. She wrote that police in the Floyd context were equivalent to “believers of ‘by any means necessary’ in achieving the goals of Zionism, similar to other terrorist groups’ missions,” while stating that “George Floyd is representative of Gazans.”  In another instance detailed by the committee, in response to a June 2025 exchange with a Jewish psychologist who wrote to leadership with grave concern about antisemitism, then-chief diversity officer Maysa Akbar replied internally, “Sigh!” Similarly, the 2021 APA president wrote “sigh………” to Akbar in response to a May 2025 letter about antisemitism from Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY). Furthermore, in spring 2025, after the medical advocacy group Do No Harm criticized antisemitism at the APA, then-senior director of strategic communications and public affairs Kim Mills wrote internally, “I wonder if the Jews who are so angry at us know they are now feeding hatred from this horrible group.”  The report also notes that in 2024, the APA avoided a request to recommend trauma psychologists for a White House screening of Screams Before Silence, a documentary about Hamas’ sexual violence on and after October 7, with one official writing, “I fear providing some names might insert us into the politics of the film and audience.”  The committee also criticized leadership’s praise of Lara Sheehi, former president of the APA’s psychoanalysis division, whose Jewish students at The George Washington University alleged in 2023 that she discriminated against them, and who has publicly claimed that Zionists have “psychosis.” After Sheehi emailed APA leaders praising their October 7 statement and claiming that those who do not recognize Israel’s “all out genocide” are experiencing “internalized racism,” 2023 APA President Thema Bryant praised Sheehi’s “heart, truth, challenge, and compassion.”  The report notes the APA continued facilitating continuing education credits for sessions led or moderated by Sheehi as recently as February 2026. According to the report, the APA has responded to concerns about antisemitism by division leaders by pointing to its bylaws, saying it “does not, and cannot, censure” members or elected or appointed officials for their speech.  Additionally, the report states that APA members turned division listservs into hostile and deeply antizionist forums after October 7, with posts defending the “humanity” of Hamas fighters and arguing Hamas deserved “kudos” for protecting civilians. In June 2026, the APA informed the House committee that it would no longer host division listservs and would instead provide an alternative online space to enhance its ability to monitor and remove content violating its policies.  Clashes over “decolonial psychology” and journal publications  The House report argues that APA leaders inflamed antisemitism by endorsing “decolonial psychology,” which the report characterizes as an academic framework that views Israel as an illegitimate settler-colonial state, justifies violent resistance, views Jews as white oppressors, and pathologizes Zionism as mental illness while demanding activism as part of clinical treatment.  In 2025, American Psychologist published a special issue on decolonial psychology, an initiative championed by Bryant. One article, titled “Supervision as Decolonial Love: Toward a Transformative Training Process for Palestinian Community Health Workers,” referred to “Palestinian freedom fighters,” described Israel as a “settler colonial” state, and claimed “Zionist psychologies” legitimize an Israeli settler-colonial project.  When the journal’s editor-in-chief later wrote to one of the authors, Devin Atallah, asking for references regarding the concept of “Zionist psychologies,” Atallah replied: “I do not have references for you on Zionist psychologies. I am also not in a place right now to be responding to general inquires [sic] – I am at capacity.” Atallah suggested the editor educate himself about antizionism “on your own.”  According to the House report, the decision to publish the “Decolonial Love” article prompted an editor for the journal’s May–June 2026 special issue on antisemitism to resign, stating the piece contained language that was “incendiary, politicized, and […] lacking the scholarly rigor we set out to uphold,” while alleging the APA was enforcing strict parameters on the antisemitism special issue that it did not apply elsewhere.  The May–June 2026 special issue of American Psychologist on “Antisemitism and Psychology” was subsequently published. As an example of the scholarship included in that edition, one peer-reviewed study examined how political liberals and conservatives evaluate individuals who express prejudice. The study found that while political liberals generally disliked prejudiced speakers more than conservatives did, liberals evaluated speakers expressing antisemitism more positively when those remarks were justified by strong disapproval of Israel or human rights concerns, viewing the speakers as politically closer to themselves and less likely to be broadly bigoted.  Jordan W. Moon of the University of Southampton, the study’s corresponding author, told PsyPost in October that the researchers found similar effects when speakers justified prejudice against Black or Chinese Americans by appealing to human rights abuses by African countries or China, describing the pattern as a general notion that prejudice is more acceptable when expressed by someone in one’s own group rather than something unique to antisemitism.  Internal battles over resolutions and a Jewish association  The House report also details internal disputes over APA resolutions. In February 2026, the APA’s Council of Representatives voted 127–37 to approve a revised Resolution on Antisemitism.  The resolution states that the APA “condemns all antisemitic attitudes and actions,” pledges to take a leadership role in opposing antisemitism, recognizes the Holocaust, and notes that antisemitic violence increased following the October 7 attacks and Israel’s subsequent invasion of Gaza. It states there is broad agreement that it is antisemitic to hold Jews collectively responsible for Israel’s actions, require Jews to publicly condemn Israel, or deny Jews in Israel/Palestine the right to exist and flourish as Jews on the basis of legal equality. It also commits the APA to including information on antisemitism in its diversity training materials.  However, the House committee criticized the measure as a “watered-down” resolution that “greenlights antisemitism,” stating that the Council of Representatives defied both the APA Board of Directors and a “Collaborative of Jewish Psychologists” formed to advise the board by voting on and passing a resolution that the Jewish advisory group never approved.  The report specifically faulted the resolution for citing the Jerusalem Declaration on Antisemitism alongside the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) definition, and for including a freestanding clause on the “weaponization of antisemitism.” That clause states that “the manipulative or bad faith invocation of accusations to silence legitimate criticism, scholarship, or activism” creates “significant adverse consequences” for Jews and non-Jews who oppose Israel’s actions and support Palestinian rights.  Simultaneously, Jewish psychologists within the APA introduced a resolution to recognize a Jewish ethnic psychological association (EPA), on par with existing affiliated EPAs for Arab, Asian American, Native American, Latino, and Black psychologists. According to the House report, APA ethnic minority groups mobilized against the effort.  The report quotes one of the main opponents of the resolution as arguing that “folks who have been conscripted into whiteness and benefitted from white privilege (whether they have collectively agreed or not) are seeking a seat and voice at the table with folks who have historically been marginalized.” Meanwhile, the APA’s Board for the Advancement of Psychology in the Public Interest (BAPPI) reported feedback from several groups that “many Jewish individuals (the majority of whom are white) do not face the same anti-Blackness, racism, white supremacy, coloniality, systemic or structural oppression as People of Color.”  BAPPI also criticized the resolution for relying on information from the ADL and for citing Sigmund Freud, who escaped Nazi Austria in 1938 and had four sisters murdered in the Holocaust, and Albert Ellis, stating their contributions to psychology “may be influenced by factors such as white/economic/male privilege.”  Additionally, the APA’s Committee on Ethnic Minority Affairs (CEMA) argued that recognizing a Jewish EPA without taking “urgent, unapologetic action on Palestine” and showing “explicit support for AMENA-Psy” would risk “reinforcing inequities and undermining solidarity across marginalized groups.”  Reaction and next steps  The House committee stated in its report that its findings will inform ongoing legislative efforts regarding discrimination by accrediting organizations.  In an October 30 statement responding to the House report, the ADL said the committee’s findings confirmed its “gravest concerns” that antisemitism is embedded in the APA’s ranks and leadership. The ADL also noted that the APA had recently delayed for the second time in 2026 a vote on recognizing the Association of Jewish Psychologists as an EPA.  “An organization devoted to the science of the mind has instead become a case study in how propaganda works, discarding facts in favor of political narratives and deepening the trauma of the Jewish psychologists among its members,” the ADL stated. “When a healing profession treats one group’s pain with such indifference, Jewish patients are right to wonder whether they will be met with compassion or with contempt.”  The ADL called on the APA to publicly condemn antisemitism, strengthen its policies and bias incident reporting mechanisms, launch an independent investigation, require antisemitism training for all leadership and staff, and recognize the Association of Jewish Psychologists as an EPA.  psypost.org/house-republican…

BREAKING EXCLUSIVE: FEC Gets Hacked, Goes Dark for 41 Hours During Early Voting with No Proof of Containment | Joe Hoft  On October 27, 2026, Reuters reported that the Federal Election Commission had taken its electronic campaign-finance filing system offline following an attempted cyber intrusion. The report quoted an email from an unnamed FEC electronic-filings officer—but did not publish the full email.  The public needs the full email, not selected portions.  The shutdown began late October 26, during early voting. Reuters subsequently reported that service returned October 28 after nearly 41 hours, interrupting new disclosures of last-minute political spending before the November 3 election.  The email contained this warning:  “We have a bad actor attempting to breach FEC systems. As a result, we’ve had to temporarily shut down our web facing services.”[hawaiitribune-herald]  Who wrote it? Who authorized the shutdown? What evidence supported the warning?  Reuters did not identify who supplied the email. Its published coverage did not reproduce the complete message, headers, attachments, or recipient list. Whether it was leaked without authorization remains unknown.  Reuters should publish the full email it reviewed. The FEC should release its authenticated original and the records explaining its response.  The agency’s listed acting chair, Shana Broussard, and its other listed serving commissioner, Dara Lindenbaum, are Democrats. The reporting reviewed does not establish when they were notified relative to outside campaign-compliance firms.[fec][fec][kentucky]  That notification timeline requires disclosure. Were agency leaders informed before outside firms? Were the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the Department of Homeland Security, or the White House notified? Was the President briefed? Which reporting requirements applied, and were they followed?  Reuters also quoted Steven Mele, president and CEO of MBA Consulting Group, about the outage’s consequences. He said he had never seen such a disruption in 26 years and warned of reduced election disclosure until service returned.[news18]  MBA provides campaign-finance compliance services. Reported clients have included Warnock for Georgia, Val Demings for U.S. Senate, Mandela Barnes for Wisconsin, Katie Porter for Congress, Catherine Cortez Masto for Senate, and Priorities USA Action. These examples come from a published client compilation, not a verified current roster.[influencewatch]  Why did Reuters select Mele, and did it sufficiently explain those relationships? Did it seek Republican compliance professionals and independent cybersecurity specialists?  His comments concerned financial disclosure—not a technical assessment of the intrusion. They cannot substitute for an official explanation of what happened. The reporting does not establish whether Mele supplied the email.[today.westlaw][news18]  The phrase “web facing services” also requires scrutiny. It describes services accessible through the internet, not every system connected behind them.  A building’s front door can be locked while an intruder remains inside. Taking a public website offline is not the same as clearing every room, checking every connecting hallway, and confirming that no other entrance remains open. The question is not which agency occupies which office. It is where an intruder could go, whether anyone got inside, and what evidence shows that access was stopped.  Federal incident-response guidance calls for isolating affected systems, revoking compromised access, and checking for ways an attacker could remain inside. If an attacker already had another foothold, unauthorized activity could continue during an outage unless containment was effective.[cisa]  CISA has also documented vulnerabilities in particular voting devices involving election-management systems or files modified before being loaded onto equipment. Reaching equipment through such a route requires specific access and vulnerabilities; it does not follow automatically from compromising a website.[cisa]  The affected FEC services handled campaign-finance filings, not ballot counting. That identifies their function—not every possible technical connection. Whether any route to election equipment existed requires evidence, not assumptions in either direction.  The public needs to know whether containment was effective—and exactly when it was achieved during the nearly 41-hour outage. What remained connected? Was unauthorized activity detected after the shutdown began? How much time elapsed between the first detected activity, the shutdown, and verified containment?  Accountability requires a public technical report documenting that timeline and the evidence supporting it. Where is that report?  Announcing that the system is back online answers a question about availability—not whether unauthorized access occurred, when it ended, or what investigators verified before restoring service.  A Freedom of Information Act request has been submit to the FEC seeking the full email, recipient list, notification records, shutdown authorizations, interagency communications, and existing technical assessments. It has not yet been filed.  joehoft.com/breaking-exclusi…

GUGULETHU SAPS MEMBERS COMMENDED FOR SWIFT ACTION IN REUNITING LOST CHILDREN WITH THEIR PARENTS  Police officers' commitment, dedication and selfless service to the community often go unnoticed. However, their efforts deserve recognition, especially when they positively impact the lives of vulnerable community members.  Last night, Friday, 06 November 2026 at approximately 18:20, two SAPS reservists, Sergeants Ruban Ngoxaza and Athenkosa Dyanti responded to a complaint involving two young children, a boy and a girl believed to be about two years old, who were found unattended in the NY111 area of Gugulethu.  The members immediately secured the safety of the children, and transported them to Gugulethu Police Station. Recognising the urgency of the situation, they promptly initiated a coordinated operation to locate the children's parents.  An operational briefing was conducted, during which all relevant role players, including members of the Crime Prevention Unit (CPU) and additional Community Service Centre (CSC) complaint vehicles were mobilised to assist in the search.  Through a coordinated effort, members conducted patrols in the Kanana, Europe and Barcelona areas of Gugulethu, utilising police vehicles equipped with blue lights and public address systems in an attempt to trace the children's parents.  Their efforts proved successful when the parents were located and the children were safely reunited with them. The reunion brought great relief and joy to the family.  This incident serves as an excellent example of teamwork, compassion, commitment and dedication to community service. It demonstrates that policing extends beyond crime prevention and law enforcement. It is also about protecting the most vulnerable members of society and making a meaningful difference in the lives of those we serve. Their swift response and coordinated efforts reflect the values of the South African Police Service and the important role police officers play in building safer communities.  SAPS management commended the members for their dedication, professionalism and commitment to serving and protecting the community.   @SAPoliceService

sample_tweets.text: IRAN TO LIFT MISSILE RANGE AND ITS POSSIBLE IMPACT PART 1   The IRGC’s November 7, 2026 announcement that the self-imposed ~2,000 km ballistic missile range limit has been lifted is confirmed and significant. It follows a directive from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (who succeeded his father Ali Khamenei after the latter’s death in the early 2026 US-Israeli strikes) for responses to threats “without geographical restrictions” and an updated target list covering US and Israeli assets. IRGC spokesman Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi stated the restriction “has been lifted for us” and that capabilities must be demonstrated on the battlefield rather than merely announced. Iran has long maintained the ~2,000–2,200 km political limit (enough to reach Israel, Gulf targets, and parts of southeastern Europe) under Ali Khamenei, even as technical capacity existed beyond it. Iran already attempted strikes on Diego Garcia (~4,000 km) in March 2026, and Iranian media/officials have recently threatened European sites (Italy, Germany, UK bases, etc.) if the US uses them for attacks on Iran. Technical and Strategic Context Iran’s core arsenal (Sejjil, Khorramshahr variants, Emad, Ghadr, etc.) is assessed around the 2,000 km class with varying payloads and accuracy. Extending range typically involves reducing warhead weight, further solid-fuel development, or leveraging space-launch technology (which can be dual-use for ICBMs). Longer-range systems would be fewer, less accurate over intercontinental distances, and more vulnerable to interception (e.g., SM-3, Aegis, Patriot, future European defenses). The move is primarily political/doctrinal signaling of deterrence and willingness to escalate beyond the region, not an immediate flood of operational ICBMs. Likely Scenarios 1.  Accelerated development and testing: Expect more investment in solid-propellant systems, possible lighter-payload extended-range variants, and tests that push ranges. Operational numbers for true long-range missiles will remain limited in the near term. Primary focus stays regional (Israel, US Gulf bases, possibly further US assets). 2.  Heightened regional escalation risk: In any renewed conflict with Israel/US, Iran can field longer-range or higher-volume salvos from deeper inside its territory. Asymmetric tools (proxies, drones, cyber, naval mining) remain central. The announcement reinforces deterrence messaging while talks remain stalled. 3.  European threat perception and responses: Southeastern Europe (Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, Cyprus) was already partially in range. Extended ranges bring more of the continent into theoretical reach. Expect tighter European missile defense investments, intelligence cooperation with the US/Israel, expanded sanctions, and greater caution about hosting US operations. Iranian threats are mostly conditional (“if you allow US bases to be used against us”), aiming to deter rather than initiate general war with Europe. Direct missile strikes on European soil would be a high-risk escalation for Tehran given NATO Article 5 implications. 4.  Nuclear dimension and broader isolation: Longer-range delivery systems amplify concerns about any nuclear breakout. This strengthens the case for maximum pressure, snapback mechanisms, or preemptive action against missile/nuclear sites. It also deepens Iran’s alignment with the Russia-China axis (technology/arms cooperation). 5.  Deterrence and diplomacy mix: Iran is signaling it will not be contained to the Middle East and will raise the costs of further strikes. This could complicate US operations or European support for them, while Iran continues asymmetric pressure and proxy activity.

Saturday Live Cattle and Feeder Cattle Outlook: The Fats & Feeders Market Outlook & News, November 7, 2026  The market finishes the first week of November with electronic paper futures staging a modest end of the week green bounce following earlier pressure, closing out Friday's session with gains across nearby cattle contracts.   Direct country cash trade held a baseline premium over futures throughout the week, with packers maintaining active bids to secure finished cattle.   Packers continue to navigate tight margin constraints, but the structural calf deficit and low placement trends keep long-term supply fundamentals firmly in focus.  Feedlot Review & Commentary The latest October USDA Cattle on Feed report delivered a distinctly bullish surprise for the livestock complex, highlighting historic low intake and persistent structural tightness:  October 1 On Feed Inventory: Total cattle and calves on feed for the slaughter market (1,000+ capacity feedlots) stood at 11.372 million head as of October 1, 2026, down 0.4% compared to October 1, 2025, coming in below trade expectations.  Record Low September Placements: Placements in feedlots during September plummeted to 1.78 million head, down 12% year over year. This marks the lowest September placement volume in series history since data collection began in 1996.  Record Low September Marketings: Marketings of fed cattle during September totaled 1.52 million head, down 6.6% year over year. This represents the lowest marketing volume for September on record, confirming ongoing gridlock in finished cattle supply.  Market Intelligence Packer margins and global demand networks set the macro backdrop for early November trade:  Slaughter Pacing: Estimated federally inspected weekly cattle slaughter ran at 430,000 head through Thursday, down 4,000 head from the prior week and trailing year-ago volumes as packers carefully manage throughput.  Long Term Herd Metrics: USDA estimates show the 2026 calf crop down 2% at 32.5 million head, maintaining a multi-decade structural low profile while heifer feedyard retention remains elevated at 37.8% of total inventory.  Cash & Country Cattle For The Week Cash Cattle Maintain Premium Baseline: Direct country trade held a clear premium over electronic paper contracts heading into the weekend. Thursday's Fed Cattle Exchange online auction reported sales at $215.00/cwt.  Cold Storage Beef Stocks Remain Lean: USDA's latest October Cold Storage report shows total frozen beef supplies in freezers down 1% from the previous month and 1% lower year over year, keeping stocks nearly 9% below five-year seasonal norms. Persistent retail procurement continues to prevent freezers from building any significant buffer heading into winter.  The "Disease Floor" & Logistics The Screwworm Factor: Livestock markets continue to monitor developments regarding the New World screwworm parasite following confirmed cattle cases in South Texas and Sonora, Mexico. Export Destination Dynamics: USDA Export Sales data showed weekly net beef business at 10,993 MT for 2026, while physical weekly shipments reached 13,441 MT marking a 17 week high. South Korea and Japan remain the leading export destinations for U.S. beef by volume and value, anchored by premium grain-fed beef demand. Globalについて、米国の金融機関が同社との資金移動を行うことを禁じる命令を出しました。2021年5月から2026年5月にかけて、制裁回避やサイバー犯罪など少なくとも160億ドル相当の不正な資金の流れに関わったと指摘しています。命令は連邦官報への掲載から30日後に施行されます。MEXC側は法務・コンプライアンス部門と対応を検討中で、運営は通常通りで利用者の資産は安全だとしています。 補足：これは制裁指定ではなく、米国の金融機関に対する資金移動の禁止命令で、利用者の口座凍結や資産の没収を命じるものではありません。160億ドルはFinCENの指摘する資金の流れの規模で、MEXCが得た利益や顧客から盗まれた金額ではありません。 出典：米財務省（公式発表・英語） home.treasury.gov/news/press… 出典：Cointelegraph（英語） 🚨 YOUR SMARTPHONE COULD BE THE NEXT TARGET OF A CYBERATTACK.   HERE’S HOW TO PROTECT IT.  With cyber threats, phishing, malware, data theft, and banking scams becoming increasingly sophisticated, protecting your smartphone is no longer optional.  Whether you use an iPhone or Android, follow these 15 security tips:  🔐 1. ALWAYS UPDATE YOUR PHONE Install the latest iOS or Android security updates. They fix vulnerabilities hackers could exploit.  🔐 2. ENABLE TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION Protect your Apple, Google, email, WhatsApp, Telegram, and financial accounts with 2FA or passkeys.  🔐 3. USE A STRONG PASSCODE Use a strong PIN or alphanumeric password, and enable Face ID or fingerprint authentication.  🔐 4. ENABLE GOOGLE PLAY PROTECT Android users should keep Play Protect enabled and scan their apps regularly.  🔐 5. CHECK APP PERMISSIONS Don’t give unknown apps unnecessary access to your camera, microphone, contacts, location, or files.  🔐 6. NEVER CLICK SUSPICIOUS LINKS Be careful with links received through WhatsApp, SMS, Telegram, email, and social media.  🔐 7. ONLY DOWNLOAD OFFICIAL APPS Use Apple’s App Store or Google Play Store. Avoid APK files from unknown websites and Telegram groups.  🔐 8. BE CAREFUL WITH PUBLIC WI-FI Avoid accessing banking services through untrusted public networks. Use mobile data or a trusted VPN when necessary.  🔐 9. ENABLE DEVICE THEFT PROTECTION iPhone: Find My + Stolen Device Protection. Android: Find Hub + Theft Protection, where supported.  🔐 10. BACK UP YOUR DATA Enable iCloud Backup or Google Backup to protect important files if your phone is lost, damaged, or compromised.  🔐 11. SECURE WHATSAPP AND TELEGRAM Enable Two-Step Verification, check linked devices, and NEVER share your OTP.  🔐 12. PROTECT YOUR MOBILE BANKING Never share your PIN, password, or OTP. Don’t install remote-access apps at someone else’s request.  🔐 13. TURN OFF UNUSED CONNECTIONS Disable Bluetooth, NFC, Wi-Fi, and Personal Hotspot when you don’t need them.  🔐 14. USE A PASSWORD MANAGER Never reuse the same password across multiple accounts. Use unique passwords and passkeys whenever possible.  🔐 15. WATCH OUT FOR AI-POWERED SCAMS Hackers can use AI to create fake bank websites, imitate voices, generate convincing emails, and impersonate people you trust.  ⚠️ IMPORTANT:  • Never share your OTP with anyone. • Never install unknown APK files. • Never scan suspicious QR codes. • Never trust unexpected investment or giveaway links. • Never ignore unfamiliar login notifications.  Remember:  Your smartphone contains your private conversations, personal photos, financial information, passwords, and access to your digital identity.  Protect your phone before someone else finds a way into it.  Sources: Apple Security, Google Security, CISA, FBI, and FTC.

Under those conditions, attacker-controlled session data can be interpreted as a serialized PHP object.  PHP Sessions | Object Injection / RCE:  CVSS: 8.1 High Attack: Remote, unauthenticated Preconditions: Specific serializer mismatch + session upload progress enabled Mitigation: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in server configuration and restart PHP workers  The PoC demonstrates the full session upload-progress chain and shows how object injection can become code execution when a usable gadget class is present in the target application.
