According to the forum post, the dataset includes a wide range of personally identifiable information (PII) and financial data fields:  *   IP addresses, first and last names *   Email addresses, city, state, zip code *   Phone numbers (primary and secondary) *   Employer names and phone numbers *   Bank name, account number, and routing number *   Social Security Number (SSN) and Date of Birth *   Driver’s license number and state *   Reference names, relationships, and phone numbers *   Occupation, shift details, direct deposit information, and work supervisor details  The SSA is an independent federal government agency responsible for administering retirement, disability, and survivor benefits to over 150 million Americans. It holds some of the most sensitive personal data in the United States, making any compromise a critical national security concern. The agency has not publicly confirmed this specific breach or data leak at the time of reporting.  The threat actor’s identity and track record remain unverified in public intelligence feeds. While the claim involves high-value federal data, no independent verification of the breach has been established. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified.  #DataLeak #SSA #SocialSecurityAdministration #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence #USGovernment #CyberSecurity

🚨 Threat Actor Claims 475k Customer Records Leaked from deercase.com  A post on an underground forum alleges that the customer database of deercase.com, a Turkish e-commerce platform, has been compromised. The threat actor claims to have extracted approximately 475,000 customer records by exploiting an unresolved vulnerability on the website.  According to the listing, the leaked data includes sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) for each customer. The exposed fields reportedly include:  - Email addresses - Phone numbers - First and last names - Account creation and update timestamps - User tags - Default shipping addresses, including street address, city, province, country, and zip code  The actor asserts that the vulnerability used to access the data remains active on the site and encourages other actors to attempt exploitation. While the specific technical details of the vulnerability are not disclosed in the post, the claim of a persistent flaw suggests a potential systemic security issue within the platform's infrastructure.  Deercase is a Turkish online retailer specializing in home goods and lifestyle products. If authentic, the exposure of full addresses and contact details for hundreds of thousands of users could facilitate targeted phishing campaigns, social engineering attacks, or physical security risks. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by deercase.com or third-party security researchers.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims 4.38 Billion Row Breach of Bullhorn  A threat actor operating under the alias "Prinz Eugen" has claimed to have breached the systems of Bullhorn, a major provider of applicant tracking systems (ATS) and talent management software. According to a post on an underground forum, the actor alleges they gained access to Bullhorn's infrastructure in October 2026 and maintained persistence for approximately two weeks before escalating privileges to enterprise administrator status within the company's Active Directory forest.  The actor claims to have exfiltrated a massive dataset comprising roughly 4.38 billion rows of SQL data and approximately 5 million documents. The post states that the stolen data is being prepared for sale in batches per company, with a threat of public release if the data is not purchased quickly. A sample file named smallsample.txt was attached to the thread to demonstrate the nature of the leaked information.  Bullhorn is a significant player in the human resources technology sector, serving thousands of staffing agencies and enterprises globally. If authentic, the exposure of such a large volume of data could compromise sensitive candidate PII, internal corporate communications, and proprietary business data for numerous client organizations relying on the platform.  Prinz Eugen is a known threat actor with a history of targeting enterprise environments through initial access brokers and credential theft. The actor has previously been associated with data theft campaigns against various industries, often leveraging compromised credentials to move laterally within networks. At the time of reporting, Bullhorn has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the alleged data leak has not been independently verified.  #DataBreach #Bullhorn #PrinzEugen #DarkWeb #HRSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Massive Breach of AU Small Finance Bank, Alleging 1.2 TB Data Leak  A threat actor has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging a significant data breach at AU Small Finance Bank, one of India's leading small finance banks. The actor claims to have compromised the bank's full database and is offering the stolen data for sale for $8,500. The post directly contradicts the bank's official statement issued in late October 2026, which attributed the incident to a limited data leak involving a third-party Salesforce SaaS platform affecting only vehicle loan customers.  The actor alleges that the bank's own core systems were breached, not just the external SaaS platform. According to the forum post, the stolen dataset totals 1.2 TB and contains over 1 billion records. The actor claims the bank is downplaying the severity of the incident to avoid regulatory scrutiny and customer panic.  The alleged compromised data includes: - 3,846,888 complete KYC identity records containing PAN, Aadhaar numbers, dates of birth, mobile numbers, emails, full addresses, and family names - 2,282,619 live customer accounts - 1,917,657 exposed bank account numbers - 938,403,770 core banking transaction and servicing records - 30,266,393 credit bureau, CIBIL, and FICO risk dossiers - 72,241,539 loan book, collateral, sanction, and insurance records - 2,871,796 signed loan agreements, scanned cheques, and customer signatures  AU Small Finance Bank, headquartered in Chennai, serves millions of customers across India with a focus on financial inclusion. The exposure of Aadhaar numbers and PAN details poses severe risks of identity theft and financial fraud for the affected individuals. The actor also provided links to sample files hosted on various file-sharing services to verify the authenticity of the dump.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified. While the bank has acknowledged a security incident related to a third-party platform, the extent of the compromise claimed by the threat actor remains unconfirmed by independent security researchers or regulatory bodies.

⚠️Threat Actor Claims 103 GB Hilton Hotel Breach on Underground Forum  A threat actor known as "BigBrother" has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging a significant data breach affecting Hilton Hotels. The post, dated November 5, 2026, asserts that the actor has compromised the hotel chain's central server, resulting in the exposure of 103 GB of data containing approximately 7,394,423 rows of customer information.  According to the listing, the stolen dataset includes personal data from Hilton Hotels customers. The actor alleges that this is their first time breaching or leaking such a target and provides a session hash as proof of access. The post does not specify the exact types of Personal Identifiable Information (PII) contained within the rows, though previous posts by this actor have involved large-scale PII dumps including national IDs and financial records.  The threat actor's track record suggests a pattern of targeting large organizations with high-value data. In September 2026, the same individual posted claims regarding massive PII leaks from Iranian institutions, including Al-Mustafa International University (89,000 records), Samaneh Khodnevis (23 million records), and HAMTA (62 million records). These prior posts were accompanied by screenshots and CSV samples, indicating a consistent methodology of offering data for sale in Bitcoin.  Hilton Worldwide is one of the largest hospitality companies globally, operating over 8,000 hotels and resorts across more than 120 countries. A breach of this magnitude, if verified, would expose sensitive guest data to potential identity theft and fraud. At the time of reporting, Hilton has not publicly confirmed the incident, and the alleged breach has not been independently verified.

🚨Moondancer Ransomware Claims Compunet Breach, Exposes 59M Rows of Mitsubishi Data  The Moondancer ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a significant cyberattack on Compunet S.A., a Colombian IT services provider, resulting in the alleged exposure of sensitive data belonging to its client, Mitsubishi Electric Colombia. According to a post on the Darkforums underground platform, the threat actor collaborated with a partner group to publish CSV dumps from Compunet’s ERP system, which reportedly contain 59 million rows and 110,000 invoices.  The post alleges that the attackers compromised more than 30 ESXi hosts and 270 virtual machines within Compunet’s infrastructure. The group claims to have encrypted 270 TB of data and deleted 60 TB of backups after negotiations with Compunet failed. The ransom note displayed in the thread addresses the CEO of Compunet directly, demanding payment or facing further data leaks.  The incident reportedly affected multiple other clients of Compunet, including: * Adama * SierraCol * Freskaleche * Ciamsa * Nutriavicola  The threat actor stated that data from these additional companies had already been sold to a private client and would not be published publicly. Compunet is a major IT solutions provider in Colombia, serving various industrial and corporate sectors. If authentic, the breach could expose operational data and financial records for numerous manufacturing and agricultural entities in the region.  At the time of reporting, neither Compunet nor Mitsubishi Electric Colombia has independently confirmed the breach or the extent of the data exposure.  #Ransomware #Moondancer #Compunet #MitsubishiElectric #DataLeak #CyberSecurity #DarkWeb

🚨 Threat Actor Claims iOS 27 Zero-Click RCE Exploit for Sale on Darkweb  A listing on an underground forum claims the availability of a zero-day remote code execution (RCE) exploit targeting Apple's upcoming iOS 27 operating system. The post, dated November 4, 2026, alleges that the vulnerability allows for root-level privilege escalation via a crafted iMessage payload without any user interaction, classifying it as a Zero-Click attack.  According to the thread, the exploit is purportedly compatible with modern iPhones and iPads running iOS 27.2 and upcoming updates. The seller describes the exploit as "very expensive" and states that only genuine buyers should make contact. While the post does not provide technical proof-of-concept (PoC) details or screenshots of the exploit in action, it explicitly mentions that escrow services are accepted for transactions.  The threat actor behind the listing has not been independently identified in this specific thread, and no prior track record was provided in the source material to verify their reputation or past activities. Claims of zero-day exploits for major mobile operating systems are frequently used as bait in underground markets; therefore, the authenticity of this specific iOS 27 vulnerability remains unverified.  If authentic, a zero-click RCE with root privileges would represent a critical security risk, potentially enabling state-sponsored actors or advanced cybercriminals to spy on high-value targets or install persistent malware undetected. At the time of reporting, Apple has not acknowledged the existence of this specific vulnerability, and the claim has not been independently verified by security researchers.  #iOS27 #ZeroDayExploit #AppleSecurity #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 Threat Actor Claims 26GB Database Breach of Argentina Federal Police  A darkweb forum post alleges that the threat actor known as SkyLing, operating under the banner of MortemTeam, has compromised the database of the Argentine Federal Police (Policía Federal Argentina, PFA). According to the listing, the actor claims to have exfiltrated a dataset totaling 26 GB from the law enforcement agency. The post, dated November 4, 2026, includes a taunting message directed at the Argentine government, stating that continued neglect of system security will result in further data exposure.  The Argentine Federal Police is a national law enforcement agency responsible for federal crimes, border control, and public order in major urban centers. As a critical government entity, it holds sensitive data related to criminal investigations, citizen records, and operational intelligence. If authentic, the exposure of such a large volume of data could potentially compromise ongoing investigations and expose personal information of citizens or personnel involved in federal cases.  SkyLing has been active on underground forums recently, targeting various government and institutional entities in Latin America. The actor’s track record includes alleged breaches of the University of Buenos Aires, the Municipality of Moreno in Argentina, and state government bodies in Mexico. In previous posts, SkyLing claimed to have dumped student records, vehicle registration data, and sensitive information from gender-based violence attention centers, often citing weak credentials or unpatched systems as the entry vector. This pattern suggests a focus on low-hanging fruit within public sector infrastructure across the region.  At the time of reporting, the Argentine Federal Police has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the authenticity of the claimed 26 GB dataset remains unverified.

Beget recovery update: 60% of shared hosting restored after destructive attack  Russian hosting provider Beget says recovery continues after the Nov 1–2 destructive attack that wiped VPS, S3 and Kubernetes data. In a Nov 5 status update it reported:  • 60% of shared-hosting servers back online (up from 35% on Nov 4) • 40% of managed dedicated servers restored (up from 15%) • 100% of unmanaged dedicated servers already running • Most VPS file-level backups survived; restoring backup servers ~24 hours, then control-panel access estimated at about five days • Billing paused while services remain unrestored  This is a material recovery UPDATE to the earlier attack, not a new incident.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Figures and timelines are Beget's own estimates, not guarantees. Hard-hit servers still need rebuilds from backups with no firm ETA. Ransomware has not been established; Beget described deletion scripts after management-plane access. Independent coverage of the same update: 1prime.ru.  t.me/beget_official/579 #CyberSecurity #CloudSecurity #IncidentResponse

🚨 RUBY ON RAILS: CRITICAL ACTIVE STORAGE FLAW (CVSS 9.8) ALLOWS UNAUTHENTICATED FILE WRITE VIA IMAGE UPLOADS  Rails has disclosed a critical flaw in Active Storage. Apps that process uploads with ImageMagick may let an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on the server with one crafted upload.  • Advisory: GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9 (no CVE yet), CVSS 9.8 • Attaching the file is enough; no variant, preview or analyze call is needed • With the Disk service, attackers may also read any file the app can read, including secret_key_base and credentials • Fixed in activestorage 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Rails does not say whether the flaw has been exploited. Upgrade now. If you store attachments with the Disk service, rotate secret_key_base, the master key and every credential the app can read.  github.com/rails/rails/secur… #DDW #DarkWeb #RubyOnRails #AppSec #PatchNow

Backdoored ARTEX Docker images pulled from Docker Hub, but installs stay at risk ⚠️  BadByte says a trojanized image of ARTEX, the AI-driven penetration testing console abused in recent bank attacks, gave anyone who knew the trick a root shell. Commands sent through the login form's captcha field ran before the password was checked.  • 7,946 pulls of tomicdd/artex and congdonglinux/artex before disclosure • 46 of 62 exposed consoles still served the backdoored build on Nov 4 • 637 GitHub repos still pointed their compose file at it • Docker removed both images on Nov 5  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Removal does not clean existing installs: any copy already pulled or cached on a mirror is still backdoored. Some things I learned working at Microsoft:  1/ large numbers everywhere. $100M ARR service isn't even a footnote on executive slide decks. Leadership time is too valuable, come back when you're $1B+. Msft ecosystem is so rich that $1B+ sales are common (it's ludicrous how much work goes into closing these). Azure has ~250 services, some are a few mil and stagnant, others in hypergrowth, some are cash cows, you see every quadrant of the growth-share matrix. Imagine the imperial navy with ships of vastly different sizes as far the eye can see  2/ more on immense scale-- the smallest of Azure services run on 10K+ VMs. Large services run on 1M+ (some maybe 10M+ VMs, idk). Msft is stamping one new datacenter into the ground every four days (!!!!), a bewildering rate. Demand is so high, even with all this buildout we're forever capacity constrained. Azure brings in $100B in revenue and is growing 40%+ annually (at this size!!) There are ~225K msft employees. You almost have to think in scientific notation, 10^4 is a tiny number here  3/ msft is totalitarian re serving the customer. It's counterintuitive to outsiders, but the warts in msft products fall out of this culture. For example, it would be easy to improve the Azure Portal. But in all my time working with customers and partners here, I haven't heard even one person complain about the portal UI. Msft invests $0.00 dollars in anything that doesn't serve the customer and is completely unapologetic about downstream implications of this mindset  4/ msft can reshape itself overnight (when it has the will). People argued whether we waited too long to adapt after Storm-0558/Midnight Blizzard hacks (with the benefit of hindsight, we definitely did). But once the leadership team privileged security, everyone's job changed in two weeks. LT tied every engineer's comp to security, centralized reporting of embedded security teams, every org reshuffled its roadmap. Within days everyone was pushing PRs with security fixes. I would have thought it inconceivable to mobilize 200K+ employees this fast  5/ Azure is complicated. Postgres depends on compute, networking, AKS (or EKS for you aws people), secrets, etc. AKS depends on compute, networking, some datastore (probably Cosmos but idk), a dozen other things. Cosmos depends on... you get the idea. When anything breaks, everything above can break too. Some construction crew accidentally cuts a fiber cable in Brazil South, or a dedicated hardware compression chip browns out in storage, or compute failure rate in west eu spikes for some reason, or a million other failure modes. Msft is relentless about improving this, idk exactly but fully loaded probably 50% of engineer time goes into resilience  6/ re lifers who work 20+ years here, SV sneers at this but I now see it differently. I was once on the bridge debugging some IO issue, we call storage, the guy diagnoses it in about a minute, we chitchat, turns out he built NT asyncio support. Or same story but with networking, the guy built NT tcp/ip stack. I used to have a boss here, we were bumping into some problem, she casually goes oh yeah, we hit that when I was working on .NET bytecode. The ex-DEC VAX/VMS database engineers built SQL Server, some are still here. I love bumping into these people  7/ I never *really* understood distribution until I got here. As an example, our team had a customer in Seoul w/ a deep performance problem. We had to fix it to unlock one of these giant contracts. We don't speak Korean, they don't speak English. Of course msft has specialists in Seoul who get to the customer site before you could even get on a plane. There is an office in every major city, a relationship with every major entity, legal experts in every jurisdiction. You can reach these ppl instantly. Claude tells me msft has ~180 offices in ~100 countries (!!) U.S. government has ~270 consulates in ~170 countries. So msft outposts aren't quite as vast as U.S. diplomatic network, but pretty vast  8/ in the 90s everyone was afraid of msft. The lore is that BillG was ruthless. He'd clone you, beat you via ecosystem/distribution strength, and moreover make the ecosystem stronger with the new product. I wasn't there to compare, but msft of today is ruthless about winning, has the will to adapt, and has the wherewithal to undertake colossal projects. Ppl see Teams bugs or whatever and completely misread the signals. Teams is less polished than Slack because msft doesn't care one iota about polish. It cares about winning, and is frighteningly good at it. Underestimate at your own risk

🚨 A PHP session handling mismatch can lead to unauthenticated object injection and remote code execution; CVE-2026-115560 PoC: https:// github.com/sykeops/CVE-2026-11 5560 The issue requires an unusual combination of PHP settings: session.serialize_handler must be configured as php_binary or php_serialize, the application must switch it to php at runtime before session_start(), and upload progress must remain enabled. Under those conditions, attacker-controlled session data can be interpreted as a serialized PHP object. PHP Sessions | Object Injection / RCE: CVSS: 8.1 High Attack: Remote, unauthenticated Preconditions: Specific serializer mismatch + session upload progress enabled Mitigation: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in server configuration and restart PHP workers The PoC demonstrates the full session upload-progress chain and shows how object injection can become code execution when a usable gadget class is present in the target application.

It never connects to the attacker directly. Every step runs on Amazon's own queue, code and notification services.
